info.title: Social Media REST API
info.description:
A complete, beginner-friendly social media backend built with **Node.js**, **Express**,
**MongoDB**, **Mongoose** and **JWT authentication**.

## What you can do

* Register and log in to receive a JWT.
* Read and update your own profile.
* Publish, read, update and delete posts (only the owner can modify a post).
* Browse users and posts with pagination.

## Authentication

1. Call `POST /api/auth/register` or `POST /api/auth/login`.
2. Copy the `token` value from the response.
3. Click the **Authorize** button, paste the token and confirm.
   Swagger UI automatically sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
4. Protected endpoints now work until the token expires.

You can also send the header manually:

```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...
```

Tokens are signed with `JWT_SECRET` and expire after `JWT_EXPIRES_IN` (default: 7 days).

## Response format

**Success**

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Post created successfully", "data": { "post": {} } }
```

**Error**

```json
{ "success": false, "message": "Something went wrong", "errors": [] }
```

`errors` is always an array. Validation errors contain `{ "field": "email", "message": "..." }`.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of public user profiles, newest accounts first.
Email addresses and passwords are never included.

**Pagination:** `?page=1&limit=10` (limit is capped at 100).
The `meta` object contains totals and next/previous page hints.

put.description:
Updates the authenticated user's own profile. No other account can be
modified with this endpoint.

**Allowed fields:** `name`, `username`, `email`, `profilePicture`, `bio`.

**Protected fields are rejected with HTTP 400:** `password`, `role`,
`isAdmin`, `_id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Send at least one allowed field.

Changing `email` or `username` checks uniqueness and returns `409`
when the value is already taken.

400.description: Validation failed or a protected field was supplied.

example.message: You cannot update protected field(s): role

delete.description:
Permanently deletes the authenticated user's account **and all posts
they created**. This action cannot be undone.

The response contains the deleted user's public profile and the number
of posts that were removed.

get.description:
Returns another user's public profile. The email address is hidden for
privacy; only the authenticated owner can see it via `/api/auth/me`.

400.description: The supplied id is not a valid MongoDB ObjectId.

errors.message: user id must be a valid MongoDB ObjectId

post.description:
Creates a post owned by the authenticated user. The author is taken
from the JWT — any `user` value in the request body is ignored.

**Required:** `content` (1–2000 characters).
**Optional:** `image` (absolute http/https URL).

put.description:
Updates the content and/or image of a post.

**Authorization:** the JWT must belong to the post's author.
Any other authenticated user receives `403 Forbidden`.

Send at least one of `content` or `image`. Sending `image: ""` removes
the image.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a post.

**Authorization:** only the post's author can delete it. Other
authenticated users receive `403 Forbidden`.

200.description: Post deleted successfully. The deleted post is returned.

errors.message: post id must be a valid MongoDB ObjectId

get.description:
Lightweight endpoint used to confirm that the API is running.
Useful for uptime monitors and for checking the connection from React.

post.description:
Creates a new account, hashes the password with bcrypt and returns a JWT.

**Required fields:** `name`, `username`, `email`, `password`.

* `email` and `username` must be unique (409 if already taken).
* `username` may contain letters, numbers and underscores (3–30 chars).
* `password` must be 8–72 characters.
* The password is **never** included in any response.

The returned token can be used immediately for authenticated requests.

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description:
Verifies the email and password and returns a signed JWT.

The same `401` message is returned for an unknown email and for a wrong
password so it is not possible to discover registered emails.

get.description:
Returns the profile of the user who owns the supplied JWT.

Send the token in the `Authorization` header:
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or use the Swagger **Authorize** button).

200.description: Current user profile. Includes the private email address.
